extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of public administration, comparative law, and political science
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and evaluative principles for designing and judging relations between state and local governments, and for determining which administrative functions should be subject to political control. Emphasizes comparative (U.S., English, Continental) experience and functional breakdown of administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant localities general (not enumerated) powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Laws should "confer upon such localities general and not detailed powers of local government."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Continental/English method grants general powers so localities can exercise them to suit local conditions; this avoids continual appeals to the legislature for new powers. Anti-pattern: the Anglo‑American practice of enumerating local powers forces localities to request frequent legislative amendments, undermining effective local self-government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject localities to central administrative control when they act as state agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Where localities act as agents for the state, their actions should be "insured by the control which the state administrative authorities... have over the actions of the local communities."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines local legislative discretion with administrative centralization so state interests are preserved while localities enjoy broad competence. Recommended as the means to secure both effective state execution and local expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely solely on constitutional prohibitions of special legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition of special legislation relative to localities has been "ineffective in securing the expression by the local communities of the local will" for multiple reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains failures: legislatures evade prohibition via minute classification (sometimes leaving single localities per class); courts often uphold such classifications as necessary for development. Thus constitutional bans alone are not a reliable method for protecting local autonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home rule (charter) protections increase local autonomy but have limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Giving larger cities the right to "draw up their own charters... which charters could not be amended nor interfered with by the state legislature" was adopted (e.g., Missouri, California) and has had more success than prohibitions of special legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caveats: courts may give a narrower meaning to 'local matters,' and permitting legislative amendment (as early California did) undermines effectiveness. Evaluate home rule by scope of charter immunity and judicial interpretation in the jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize necessity of some state control to avoid fragmentation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Local communities cannot... be removed entirely from the control of the state. State disintegration would follow if this were done."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any plan to limit legislative control must provide another legitimate state authority to exercise oversight. Removing legislative control without a substitute invites disintegration and has been resisted by legislatures and courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for the partisan political system's effects on local autonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: The partisan party system tends to develop "extraordinary strength" and often sacrifices local interests to state or national issues; parties will intervene in localities to secure enforcement of state-wide policies (e.g., prohibition enforcement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating local autonomy, consider party incentives and the role of state/national parties in local elections; strong state parties can swamp local voices, whereas urban voting strength may force parties to formulate local policies or cede to municipal parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiation of local from state will requires both administrative centralization and legislative decentralization
rubrics_metrics.description: "The centralization of administration so necessary... has been accompanied by a decentralization in legislation without which there can be no opportunity for the expression of a local will."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended model: centralize administrative control (to secure state interests/execution) while decentralizing legislative detail (granting localities general powers). Also depends on enlightened public opinion insisting on proper state-local relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze administration by distinct functions (justice vs government)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administration may be "either of justice or of government." The administration of justice (interpretation of state will) should be made by an authority relatively independent of the legislature (judicial authority).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this functional distinction to decide appropriate institutional placement and insulation from politics. The judicial/interpretive side should be removed from political control; other administrative functions require separate treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and protect quasi-judicial and technical administrative functions from political control
rubrics_metrics.description: Many administrative duties (assessing property values, approving building plans, statistical work, registration, information gathering) require technical knowledge and should be treated as quasi‑judicial or quasi‑scientific and be "absolutely impartial and as free from prejudice as possible."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such functions are ill-suited to ordinary political control because political interference cannot produce better technical judgments or more exact facts. Ensure permanence, technical competence, and impartiality for agencies performing these tasks. Anti-pattern: subjecting technical adjudication and fact‑gathering to partisan manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subordinate the executive (law‑execution) function to political control
rubrics_metrics.description: "The function of executing the law... must therefore of necessity be subordinated to the function of politics."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because execution of law requires coordination with the lawmaking body and may involve refusal to execute if independent, executive agencies should be politically accountable/subordinated to maintain harmony between lawmaking and execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election administration must be impartial to preserve popular government
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions preliminary to choice of officers and election conduct must be "as impartial and free from prejudice as possible" so elected officers will represent the people and government will be popular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design election administration to minimize partisan discretion and protect fairness; failures (e.g., partisan selection of election officials or fraudulent registration) justify judicial remedies like mandamus in some jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasi‑judicial discretion generally shields officers from action for motives, but bad faith remains actionable
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts have held that discretionary quasi‑judicial powers are judicial in character and exempt officers from action for motives; yet there is a tendency to hold non‑court officers responsible for bad faith or dishonest purposes (cases cited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating administrative discretion, recognize the general immunity for discretionary quasi‑judicial acts but also the limits where fraud, bad faith, or partisan abuse can create liability or judicial intervention (e.g., mandamus, tort liability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnose U.S. failures to secure state‑local differentiation by three causes
rubrics_metrics.description: The causes of comparative failure in the United States are: (1) the legislative habit of enumerating local powers, (2) the locality's role as an agent of state government, and (3) the position assigned to political parties by the governmental system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these three diagnostic dimensions when assessing reforms: reduce harmful enumeration, rework agent relationships, and adjust party incentives or structures to better enable local will expression.
